historical_state_model.meaning: A singleton defect orbit is the only accumulated pair obligation violated by that verified historical state. Omitting it permits that exact pair-failure family to recur.

selection_rule.name: historical-core
selection_rule.algorithm: Protect pair orbits that occur alone in any historical defect set, then greedily cover the remaining historical sets; break ties by singleton multiplicity, impact, recurrence, and stable orbit order.
selection_rule.soundness: Every omitted pair, triple, and quadruple obligation remains subject to the exact lazy audit before GCTS can begin.

matched_seeds_325_to_327.result: Protecting every singleton orbit is 31.3% slower in aggregate and leaves 36.4% more pair defects than ordinary historical coverage. It does expose one previously unseen pair orbit, so it remains an optional diversity lane rather than a production replacement.

warning: Historical-core is finite-state proposal steering. It is not a tiling, non-tiling, or aperiodicity certificate.
